scope: P1.3 producer shared-memory publication, not complete decoder/backend/clock qualification
technology_decision: Use the native CPython writable buffer interface with existing OpenCV isolation: producer byte-copy median CPU799.819ms to0.501ms, exact parity. This replaces per-byte ctypes assignment without a new ABI/runtime; no allocation reduction claimed.
alternatives: GStreamer appsink provides bounded queue controls and PyAV exposes video frames/planes, but either whole-decoder replacement still needs independent device/timestamp/stride and deployment qualification. This measured boundary improvement does not choose or grandfather the full backend.

checks.hosted: Six installed publication tests and producer comparison added to existing edge contracts jobs; pending

limitations: Injected backend tests exercise real _decode publication/read, not real device/codec behavior. Existing three-OS real-codec jobs also run for the delivery head.
Previous local file-codec startup failure remains unproven; no unchanged local rerun.
CPU is diagnostic shared-Mac process time, not end-to-end capture latency or hard real-time qualification.
Native video conversion and owned byte creation still allocate; only the subsequent shared-buffer assignment changed.
Exposure trust, lock boundary, sequence/provenance, size limits and source fault codes preserved.
